items.headline: Cherki and Declan Rice headline a 20.5-goal gamble in 21 Goals
items.summary:
The challenge in 21 Goals is not to chase the biggest scorer, but to land as close as possible to 21 combined goals from four players without going over. That makes Erling Haaland a season-wrecking pick rather than a safe one: one prolific forward can bust the whole entry on his own.

The proposed lineup starts with Rayan Cherki, the Manchester City attacker, who is projected at around seven goals. The appeal is that much of his fantasy value should come through creativity and assists rather than a huge goal tally, keeping him useful without threatening the 21-goal cap.

Juju Behaul is the second pick, pencilled in for roughly five or six goals, before Gabriel is added as a steadier low-ceiling option. Gabriel is backed to deliver his familiar return of about three goals across the season, giving the squad a secure base rather than too much volatility.

With the first three players estimated at around 15 or 16 goals, the final slot goes to Declan Rice. He is seen as capable of adding four or five goals, taking the total projection to about 20.5 — close enough to maximise upside, but still just under the bust line. The game is set-and-forget: pick the four-man lineup at the start of the season, with no weekly transfers or captaincy calls, and entries can join a mini-league using code 50QF3R1.

Erling Haaland is treated as a trap because his goal volume is too high for the format.

The logic is simple: if the bench is not carrying dead spots or long-term punts, the opening weekend can be used to cash in before early-season price changes, rotation patterns and transfers make squads messier.

That chip plan shapes the final two selection calls. The remaining forward slot needs to be cheap, and while Wissa is acknowledged as tempting at Newcastle, the preference is to avoid him for this specific structure. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the planned pick instead, with his underlying data and longer-term fixture run making him the stronger fit beyond just Gameweek 1.

The final goalkeeper place comes down to a 4.5m option to pair with Kinsky. With exactly 4.5m left, Verbruggen is the preferred choice because the other candidates in that bracket do not offer as attractive a Gameweek 1 fixture for a bench boost. The emphasis is not only on season-long value, but on making sure every bench slot has a realistic chance of returning immediately.

The squad is therefore considered close to locked ahead of the deadline: Kinsky and Verbruggen as the goalkeeper pairing, Calvert-Lewin filling the cheap forward role, and the bench boost still on the table because the bench is being constructed for minutes rather than just budget cover.

items.headline: Haaland captains a Gameweek 1 Bench Boost squad, with Bruno Fernandes the live alternative
items.summary:
The Gameweek 1 squad is set up for an immediate Bench Boost, built around cheap rotation in goal, a value-heavy defence and a familiar premium attack. Bart Verbruggen starts with Kinski on the bench, a low-cost goalkeeper pairing that rotates well enough to justify using the chip early. The bench is not an afterthought: Gomes, O’Shea and Ballard are all included as value picks who make the Bench Boost viable rather than a forced play.

Defence is deliberately trimmed back to just one Arsenal player, a compromise that feels uncomfortable but is shaped by uncertainty around the Konsa transfer situation and the appeal of cheaper routes to upside. Calvin Bassey is preferred at 5.5 because he is seen as the most attacking option in that bracket, while Rico Williams returns to the draft thanks to strong fixtures in Gameweeks 1, 3 and 5. Harry Maguire is also included as a long-running goal threat punt, with the hope that his set-piece threat finally converts into FPL points.

In midfield, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are treated as locks, with the squad aggressively targeting their opening two fixtures. Dominik Szoboszlai is picked as a balanced midfielder with multiple routes to returns, while Pascal Groß is included on the assumption that he may retain penalty duties. The key captaincy call remains Erling Haaland, who currently has the armband, though Fernandes is close enough to create genuine temptation for Gameweek 1.

The forward line of Haaland, João Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin is common but hard to oppose on structure and value. If Gomes is not available, an alternative no-João Pedro build brings in Brobby instead, freeing funds to upgrade Gomes to Enjoi and likely setting up a Gameweek 4 wildcard. A more aggressive route is also on the table: going without Haaland entirely and planning an early Gameweek 3 wildcard, though that carries far greater risk given Haaland’s captaincy appeal.

The risks are just as clear: he may rarely play 90 minutes, he is new to this Arsenal role, the fixtures quickly stiffen after Coventry, and a blank could make him an immediate sell. Liverpool’s midfield also drives much of the debate. Dominik Szoboszlai is the more pragmatic pick: £0.5m cheaper, likely to play 90 minutes, involved in set pieces, capable of defensive contributions from the double pivot and potentially moving into the No 10 role when Wirtz is withdrawn. The midfield is built around the idea that if Bruno is omitted, some Manchester United attack is still essential, making Bryan Mbeumo a must-have despite a slight concern after he was benched in the last friendly. Dominik Szoboszlai, Antoine Semenyo and Kevin Schade join him, with Schade boosted by Brentford’s seven-goal preseason performance. Arsenal’s 6.5m Salisu completes the midfield.

Up front, the money saved on Bruno goes directly into Haaland alongside João Pedro, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin available from the bench. The guiding principle is clear: either build around Bruno and go without Haaland, or skip Bruno and make Haaland the premium focal point, while using the extra balance to create a squad deep enough for an early bench boost.

items.summary:
Arsenal’s late defensive news changes the Gameweek 1 setup. Ezri Konsa is expected to join from Aston Villa, while Jurrien Timber is now reportedly closer to a September return, making Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White less secure beyond the first couple of gameweeks. Mosquera and White are still expected to start against Coventry in Gameweek 1, and probably at Aston Villa in Gameweek 2, but disruption can begin from Gameweek 3. Gabriel and David Raya look like the safe Arsenal routes, while Riccardo Calafiori remains appealing for his attacking upside despite some substitution risk. Konsa is a possible 4.5m long-term route into Arsenal, but not for a Gameweek 1 Bench Boost because his immediate start is not assured.

The preferred squad is built for a Gameweek 1 Bench Boost and keeps flexibility for an early Wildcard, most likely around Gameweek 4. In goal, Verbruggen and Kinsky are the 4.5m pair. Defence is light on Arsenal with only Calafiori, supported by Harry Maguire, Nico Williams, Dan Ballard and O’Shea. Maguire is close to locked because of his goal threat and fixtures, Williams has attractive home games around a Liverpool away fixture that can be avoided, and Ballard is a short-term Sunderland pick for defensive-contribution potential and set-piece threat. The concern is that this defence turns quickly by Gameweek 4, which may force the Wildcard.

Midfield centres on Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo for Manchester United’s opening run against Hull and Ipswich. Fernandes is fixed in the team and is already the Gameweek 2 captain, while Mbeumo’s preseason benching is not considered a major issue; he is still expected to start as the number nine in the short term, although his minutes and role may become less secure once Cunha, Sesko and European rotation come into play. Szoboszlai is considered a near-lock because of security, set pieces and possible penalty upside. Pascal Gross stays for now at 5.5m, but his appeal weakens if Brighton signing Promise David takes penalties. Diego Gomez is the preferred 5.0m midfielder if fitness and European minutes confirm he is ready, with George Hemings a cheaper emergency alternative.

Up front, the template trio of Erling Haaland, Joao Pedro and Dominic Calvert-Lewin remains the preferred route. Haaland is in largely because of captaincy in Gameweeks 3, 5 and 7 against Coventry, Sunderland and Middlesbrough, though his Gameweek 1 minutes may be managed and Bruno Fernandes is a live captaincy alternative. Joao Pedro is not viewed as essential for the first two weeks, especially with Arsenal away in Gameweek 3, but his ownership, role as Chelsea’s number nine and long-term value make him hard to omit. Calvert-Lewin is favoured among 6.0m forwards because he offers the clearest mix of first-choice striker status, minutes and penalties.

Two alternative builds remain on the table. If Gomez is not viable, Joao Pedro can become Brobbey for the first three gameweeks, allowing Gomez to become Ndiaye and a defender upgrade such as Ajer or Ben White, but that means fading Joao Pedro’s huge ownership. The more aggressive route removes Haaland entirely, captains Fernandes in Gameweek 1, adds Isak up front and loads up on Arsenal defence with Raya, Gabriel and Calafiori before Wildcarding in Gameweek 3 to buy Haaland and Manchester City assets for Coventry. That no-Haaland draft rates well because it spreads budget across the squad, but it carries obvious risk if Haaland starts fast against Bournemouth.

Bryan Mbeumo remains a strong Gameweek 1 pick despite not starting Manchester United’s final friendly, with the absence treated as rest rather than a warning sign. He fits the short-term “Haaland switch” structure and can be reassessed after two gameweeks, when Liverpool midfielders, Palmer, Semenyo, Rogers or Sarr-style moves may become clearer. Bruno Fernandes is still central to drafts and even carries the armband in one final squad build, while Haaland, Joao Pedro and Calvert-Lewin form the preferred forward line.

Bench Boost timing is still the biggest structural fork. Bench Boost 1 drafts lean on immediate playable cheap assets such as Sangare, Rodon and Diop, while Bench Boost 2 opens up combinations involving Van Hecke, Ampadu, Bobby Thomas and Coventry coverage. Sangare is preferred to Pascal Gross among the £5.5m midfielders because defensive contributions look more repeatable than relying on Brighton penalties and set pieces, especially with Brighton’s new striker potentially affecting penalty duties. items.headline: No-Haaland Gameweek 1 draft loads up on Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal defence and bench boost depth
items.summary:
A Gameweek 1 squad without Erling Haaland frees up enough money to build a much deeper Fantasy Premier League team, with the main argument resting on value, form and early chip strategy. Haaland’s £15.5m price tag is questioned after his Community Shield display, and the draft leans into a Bench Boost in Gameweek 1 to maximise points across all 15 players rather than concentrating budget in one premium forward.

The goalkeeper pairing remains Bart Verbruggen and Kinski, mainly because they rotate well and both help support the opening-week Bench Boost plan. In defence, the extra Haaland money allows more spending: Gabriel comes in at £8.0m, joined by Riccardo Calafiori, who could alternatively be Ben White, and Harry Maguire. Diop and Muharemovic sit on the bench but are still intended to contribute in Gameweek 1 if the chip is active.

Midfield is where the no-Haaland structure starts to look powerful. Bruno Fernandes is treated as close to essential in this setup, with the point made that managers may not want to go without both him and Haaland, but dropping one of the two enables a much stronger all-round squad. Bryan Mbeumo, Antoine Semenyo, Arsenal’s popular new £6.5m signing Soucek, who has supplied plenty of pre-season assists, and Liverpool’s Dominik Szoboszlai complete a well-funded midfield.

Up front, the draft goes with Joao Pedro, Thiago and Dominic Calvert-Lewin instead of Haaland. The appeal is that all three look sharp and arguably enter the season in better form than the Manchester City striker. The clear risk is Gameweek 3, when Haaland has Coventry at home, so this route requires either a plan to buy him back or the nerve to bet against him through an attractive early fixture.
